entrypoints.host: JSON Lines op=trace with optional startStep, maxSteps and maxTensorBytes

result_class: TracedMultiInputRun has a generated private constructor in the TypeScript surface; callers receive it from runWithTrace and read report() or output()

bounds.start_step: zero-based index within the compiled steps
bounds.max_steps: 1..=256; the window is truncated at the last step

digest.bytes: flat f32 values in tensor order, each IEEE-754 bit pattern encoded little endian
digest.scope: exact observed tensor values, not tensor shape, graph identity or authorization
digest.skipped_digest: null with explicit capture_status and byte_length when available

trace_complete_meaning: all compiled step indices were observed and the graph completed; some tensor digests may still be null due to capture bounds

failure.preflight_or_invalid_bounds: error before graph execution; no trace object or receipt
failure.numerical_step: report execution_status=failed, fault_step_index, error and completed prefix; output() fails
failure.host_numerical_step: ok=false and execution_trace in JSON Lines response; no execution receipt
failure.durable_host: a failed numerical run discards the active session, and a successful traced run commits an execution receipt under the same ledger lock

limits: Observations materialize tensors for hashing and can add CPU time and memory use; they do not replace the Burn operator result.
A window observes its selected indices while all preceding and subsequent graph steps still execute.
A trace is one execution; calling run separately executes the graph again and may change mutable state.
A digest identifies exact f32 bytes only; it is not a signature or action permission.
For a completed durable host trace, compare terminal_output.value_sha256 with execution_receipt output digest when captured.
